Vanessa —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of BrightBank's SIG review we need a short package that clarifies Redwood's vulnerability management retention and remediation routing. Specifically we need:

- Scan cadence (authenticated/internal + unauthenticated/external) and how long raw scan artifacts and exports are retained.
- SLA by severity for CVE remediation and how exceptions are routed/approved.
- Proof that fixes were applied (patch manifests or deployment IDs) for any CVEs closed in the last 12 months.
- Clarification on third-party dependency scanning and retention for vendor-supplied components.

Can you confirm whether a 12-month retention window for raw scan artifacts and the remediation matrix we requested is available? If so, please share the artifacts and a short signed attestation we can include in the SIG packet. Ideally we need this by COB 2026-10-11.

If you prefer, we can accept a single compressed bundle and a signed DocuSign attestation. Let me know the expected delivery and whether you need a GAP window.

Thanks,
Erin Caldwell
Security Auditor, BrightBank

Erin —

Thanks, we can provide what you outlined. Quick summary up-front:

- Scan cadence: authenticated internal scans run weekly; external unauthenticated scans run nightly.
- Retention: raw scan exports and historical scan reports retained for 14 months by default (longer retention available on request).
- CVE remediation SLA: Critical (7 days), High (30 days), Medium (90 days), Low (180 days); exceptions handled via an internal compensating control review and approved by Security Ops.
- Third-party dependency scanning: we run SCA at least weekly and include vendor-supplied dependency manifests in the same retention window.

I've attached the following artifacts for your review: vm-scan-index.csv (metadata for the last 12 months), cve-closure-matrix.xlsx (mapping: CVE -> owner -> ticket -> patch/deploy ID), and a short policy extract (scan-retention-policy.pdf).

Next steps: can you confirm that a single ZIP of these files plus a DocuSign signature will be accepted? If yes, I'll route the DocuSign to you and provide the ZIP via the Drive link below.

Delivery commitment: we can upload the bundle to the Drive folder and send DocuSign for signature by EOD 2026-10-06. If you need the signed attestation earlier, please tell me and we'll prioritize.

Vanessa — quick technical addendum to include in the response (feel free to paste as a short appendix):

- SCANNER STACK / CADENCE:
  * Internal auth scans: Tenable.io credentialed scans against defined asset groups, weekly.
  * External unauthenticated scans: Nessus/Qualys nightly perimeter scans, nightly for public-facing surfaces.
  * SCA: Snyk scans of CI/CD builds and dependency manifests, weekly.

- RETENTION & ARTIFACTS:
  * Raw scan exports (Nessus XML / Tenable CSV) retained for 14 months in our secure artifact store (immutable backups for the first 90 days) and accessible to auditors with a signed request.
  * Aggregated reports (PDF/CSV) retained for 36 months for compliance reporting.

- REMEDIATION ROUTING / SLAS:
  * Triage: auto-create ticket in JIRA SECOPS- board, severity assigned by the triage rule.
  * Ownership: dev or infra team assigned; security owns exceptions.
  * SLA: Critical = 7 calendar days (hotpatch window + verification), High = 30 days, Medium = 90 days, Low = 180 days.
  * Exceptions: documented in JIRA with compensating control description; approvals logged in the ticket and mirrored to our audit ledger (JIRA link included).

- PROOF OF FIXES:
  * We include: ticket ID, deploy job ID (CI build), kube rollout/AMI version, and post-patch scan evidence (simple delta report).

Notes: for third-party vendor components where we cannot patch upstream, we provide mitigation artifacts & exception records and include CVSS/time-to-fix rationale.

Kimberly Park
Director, Vulnerability Management
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Vanessa / Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. The 14-month retention for raw exports and the SLA table look acceptable for our SIG packet. A couple of clarifications before we close the item:

1) For vendor-supplied components where patching is not controlled by Redwood, please include the most recent evidence of the compensating control (config, WAF rule, isolation) and the exception ticket ID.

2) For proof of fixes, our review prefers deploy job IDs + post-patch delta scan when available. The CVE matrix you sent looks like it includes deploy IDs — perfect.

Please send the ZIP through the Drive folder and route the DocuSign attestation to audits@brightbank.com (we'll sign on receipt). COB 2026-10-11 is fine; if you can deliver earlier (by 2026-10-06 as proposed), that helps our audit sprint.
